title: Borrow Yourself
goal: cost() gets called twice on the same package. Choose the self that survives.
hints: The test calls cost() twice on the same value.
Taking self by value consumes the package on the first call.
explanation: `self` by value consumes the package: the first `p.cost()` moves it, and the second is E0382, use of moved value. `&self` borrows instead - the method reads the weight and hands the package back. Naming the parameter `this` breaks the `self.weight` in the body (E0424: self only exists for self parameters). The rate must stay an integer: `3.0` is E0277 against a u32.
